finding.claim: iconUrl is stored with no validation and later fetched by the nightly sync job, so a user can make the server issue GET requests to any URL, including internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: The `icon` parameter of Profile.update (PUT /profile), line 11. It is user-controlled.

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) receives the user-supplied icon.
this.iconUrl = icon is stored with no check. Only the webhook is validated, at line 12.
The nightly sync passes URI.create(iconUrl) to c.send as a GET, and the response body is read with ofByteArray().

finding.guards_checked: The regex at line 12 checks only `webhook`, not `icon`. There is no scheme, host or IP allowlist, no private-address check, and no connect-time pinning on the path. The HttpClient `c` is passed in and its configuration is not visible here. The webhook sink at line 21 is safe: String.matches requires a full match, the dot is escaped, and the host is fixed to hooks.example.com. The path is a fixed 20-character alphanumeric token, so it cannot be redirected to another host. The client's redirect policy is not visible; HttpClient does not follow redirects by default, so a redirect from the fixed host would not change this finding.

verdict.reason: src/Profile.java:16 stores the user-supplied `icon` unvalidated (the regex at line 12 only checks `webhook`), and src/Profile.java:23 sends a GET to URI.create(iconUrl), with no other callers or guards in the codebase.
